title: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.37523v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A persistent belief in modern AI is that sufficiently large learners trained on sufficiently much data can make explicit domain knowledge optional. This paper examines a limitation of that belief. We define structure-encoded problems: tasks whose input-output map is determined, or sharply constrained, by known structure such as a solver, symmetry group, graph, physical law, measurement operator, grammar, combinatorial search space, or optimization objective. For such tasks, the central question is not expressivity--a dense neural network may contain the desired map--but finite-data identification, extrapolation, and certification. We introduce the structure gap: the finite-resource gap between a method that receives the governing structure and a learner that receives only examples. translated_title: 结构差距：当更多数据无法取代结构化推理时
translated_abstract: 现代人工智能中存在一种根深蒂固的信念：在足够多数据上训练的足够大的学习器可以让显式的领域知识变得可有可无。本文考察了这一信念的一个局限性。我们定义了结构编码问题：即其输入输出映射由已知结构（如求解器、对称群、图、物理定律、测量算子、文法、组合搜索空间或优化目标）所决定或严格约束的任务。对于此类任务，核心问题不在于表达能力——稠密神经网络可能已经包含所需的映射——而在于有限数据下的辨识、外推与认证。我们提出了结构差距的概念：即获得支配性结构的方法与仅获得样本的学习器之间在有限资源下的差距。这一论断最有用的最强形式是渐近性的而非绝对性的：随着覆盖范围的增长，结构无关的学习可能逼近结构化求解器（原文摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 本文提出“结构差距”这一概念，指出对于由求解器、物理定律等已知结构决定或约束的任务，纯数据驱动的学习器在有限资源下无法通过增加数据完全替代结构化推理，其差距集中体现在有限数据辨识、外推与认证能力上。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "structure gap"—the finite-resource gap between methods that receive the governing structure and learners that only see examples—showing that for structure-encoded tasks, more data alone cannot replace structured reasoning in finite-data identification, extrapolation, and certification.
